title: Comparison
description: Output of `ocr-eval compare`. Turns two runs into a decision (FR-008, SC-006). A comparison only exists when the two runs are commensurable on all four counts: same policy_version, same corpus_manifest_digest, same split set, same page set. Otherwise the command exits 3 and writes nothing.

delta.description: candidate - baseline. Sign alone is never the reader's only cue — see direction.

direction.description: Stated as a word because the sign that means 'better' differs per metric: lower is better for CER, higher for exact_match_rate.

outcome_changed.description: e.g. 'scored -> hallucination'. null when the contract outcome is the same on both sides.

policy_version.description: Identical in both runs, or the comparison does not exist.

primary_split.description: The split the PROMOTE rule reads. Default synthetic_heldout.

verdict.description: A REJECT is a successful comparison, not a failed command: the process still exits 0 and scripts read the verdict from here, not from the exit code.

verdict_reasons.description: Every rule that fired, in rule order. Never empty — an INCONCLUSIVE verdict states why it is inconclusive, so a reviewer can act without opening the underlying data (SC-006).

thresholds.description: The rule as applied, echoed so the verdict is reconstructable later.

promote_min_cer_improvement_pp.description: Default 0.5 percentage points absolute, strict micro CER on the primary split.

reject_on_any_gold_regression.description: Default true. Encodes the project's real risk: synthetic gains that do not survive real scans.

splits.description: Per split, every headline metric on both sides with its delta and direction. Sorted by split name. No cross-split total, for the same reason as in run-summary (FR-013). metrics contains only those metrics defined on BOTH sides: a split whose scored_pages is 0 has a null headline in run-summary (research R-018) and so contributes only its contract rates here, never a delta computed from a null. Whether a split is scoreable is a property of the corpus rather than of the model, and the two runs are already guaranteed the same corpus and the same page set, so scored_pages always agrees between them and a metric is never present on one side alone.

bootstrap.description: Paired bootstrap over per-page CER deltas, so a 0.4-point improvement that straddles zero is visibly not a result. Deterministic: fixed seed, recorded.

confidence.description: Fixed at 95%. Pinned because nothing in configs/eval/default.json can change it.

resamples.description: Echoed from config key bootstrap_resamples, default 10000. Deliberately not pinned to a const: the config is tunable and every threshold in force is echoed into the artifact, so a const would make any non-default run fail its own schema.

seed.description: Echoed from config key bootstrap_seed, default 20260916. Not pinned, for the same reason as resamples. Its presence is what makes the interval reproducible; its value is a choice, not a constant.

regressions.description: Pages that got worse, sorted by delta_cer descending then page_id (FR-008 scenario 2). Truncated to --top.

improvements.description: Pages that got better, sorted by delta_cer ascending then page_id. Truncated to --top.

only_in_baseline.description: Page ids present in the baseline run only. Always empty in a produced artifact: an unequal page set is the fourth incommensurability condition, so the command names the offending ids on stderr and exits 3 instead of writing this file (research R-004). Kept as a required, always-empty field so a consumer can assert emptiness rather than infer it.

only_in_candidate.description: As above, for the candidate run.

verdict_reasons: strict micro CER on synthetic_heldout improved by 6.20pp (>= 0.50pp required for PROMOTE)
